question_en: You are invited to a German colleague's home for dinner at 19:00. When should you arrive?
options: (A) About 15 minutes early to show respect
(B) Exactly at 19:00 or within 5 minutes after
(C) 30 minutes late is fashionable
(D) Any time before 20:00 is fine

question_en: When addressing a German colleague you just met professionally, which form should you use?
options: (A) Use 'du' (informal) immediately to be friendly
(B) Use 'Sie' (formal) until invited to use 'du'
(C) Use first name only without any pronoun
(D) There is no distinction in modern German

question_en: Why are most shops closed on Sundays in Germany?
options: (A) Most Germans prefer online shopping on Sundays
(B) It is mandated by Ladenschlussgesetz (closing law) and Sonntagsruhe (Sunday rest) tradition
(C) Shops are simply unprofitable on Sundays
(D) This practice no longer exists

question_en: In a German apartment building, what is 'Ruhezeit'?
options: (A) A weekly cleaning schedule for residents
(B) Mandated quiet hours (typically 22:00-06:00 and Sundays) when loud activities are prohibited
(C) A neighborhood watch program
(D) A traditional German tea time

question_en: Why do Germans NOT wish someone happy birthday BEFORE their actual birthday?
options: (A) It is considered bad luck (vorgratulieren) and may bring misfortune
(B) German calendars are different from international ones
(C) It is illegal under German tradition law
(D) This superstition does not actually exist

question_en: When toasting with drinks in Germany, what is essential etiquette?
options: (A) Down the drink in one shot
(B) Maintain eye contact while clinking glasses and saying 'Prost'
(C) Touch glasses with everyone twice
(D) Pour the drink for yourself first

question_en: What is the Reinheitsgebot in German beer culture?
options: (A) A modern marketing slogan invented in the 2000s
(B) The Beer Purity Law (1516) limiting beer ingredients to water, hops, malt (and later yeast)
(C) A German beer festival held annually in Berlin
(D) The legal drinking age in Germany

question_en: In Germany, what do you typically receive on your first day of school?
options: (A) A school uniform set
(B) A Schultüte — a large decorated cone filled with candy and school supplies
(C) A bouquet of flowers from the teacher
(D) Nothing special, just a regular school day

question_en: Why is cash still preferred over cards in many German establishments?
options: (A) German banks do not support card payments
(B) Strong cultural preference for privacy, financial control, and skepticism of debt
(C) Card readers are illegal in small businesses
(D) Card payments are taxed much higher

question_en: What is 'Pfand' in German consumer culture?
options: (A) A type of traditional bread
(B) A deposit on bottles and cans, refunded when returned for recycling
(C) A government tax on imported goods
(D) A discount card for grocery stores

question_en: When a German says they will 'think about it', what does this typically mean?
options: (A) They are politely declining without saying no
(B) They genuinely intend to consider it seriously
(C) They are angry and ending the conversation
(D) They want you to ask three more times

question_en: What does 'Mahlzeit' mean and when is it used?
options: (A) Goodbye, used only when leaving work
(B) A casual greeting around lunchtime, meaning 'enjoy your meal' or simply hello
(C) An apology for being late
(D) A request for the bill in restaurants

question_en: In Germany, why is direct verbal feedback common in professional settings?
options: (A) Germans are inherently rude by other standards
(B) Direct communication is valued as honest, efficient, and respectful of others' time
(C) German employers legally require harsh criticism
(D) It is only done with strangers, never colleagues

question_en: What is 'Polterabend' in German wedding tradition?
options: (A) The honeymoon trip after the wedding
(B) Pre-wedding party where guests smash porcelain for good luck (couple cleans up together)
(C) A formal engagement ceremony
(D) The first dance at the wedding reception

question_en: Why do many Germans take off their shoes when entering a home?
options: (A) It is required by German hygiene law
(B) Common practice for cleanliness, especially in northern Germany; varies by household
(C) Only practiced in rural areas, never cities
(D) This custom does not exist in Germany

question_en: What is 'Strandkorb' that you might see on German beaches?
options: (A) A type of beach umbrella
(B) A hooded wicker beach chair providing shelter from wind, often rented
(C) A beach volleyball court
(D) A German seafood dish

question_en: Why are Germans famous for their bread culture (Brotkultur)?
options: (A) Bread is the only carbohydrate available in Germany
(B) Over 3,000 registered bread varieties; UNESCO-recognized intangible cultural heritage
(C) Germans only eat bread for every meal
(D) Bread was banned during WWII and is now celebrated

question_en: In German workplace culture, what is the typical attitude toward overtime?
options: (A) Frequent overtime signals dedication and is encouraged
(B) Working strict hours is respected; excessive overtime may signal poor planning
(C) Overtime is mandatory in all German companies
(D) Germans work the longest hours in Europe

question_en: What is 'Ausbildung' in the German education system?
options: (A) Compulsory military training for young men
(B) Vocational dual training combining classroom learning with paid apprenticeship
(C) A type of university entrance exam
(D) Adult education for retirees

question_en: Why do Germans typically eat their main meal at lunch (Mittagessen) rather than dinner?
options: (A) Restaurants are closed in the evening
(B) Traditional preference for hot, substantial lunch and lighter cold dinner (Abendbrot)
(C) Tax laws encourage daytime spending
(D) This is no longer practiced anywhere

question_en: What does 'FKK' refer to in German culture?
options: (A) A type of formal handshake
(B) Freikörperkultur — nude/clothing-optional swimming and sunbathing tradition
(C) A government health insurance program
(D) A German fast-food chain

question_en: In Germany, asking about someone's salary is generally considered:
options: (A) Standard small talk at any social event
(B) Quite private and intrusive; usually avoided
(C) Required when meeting new people
(D) A compliment to their professional status

question_en: Why is Germany known for elaborate recycling (Mülltrennung)?
options: (A) Germans have nothing else to do with their time
(B) Strict environmental policies with separate bins for paper, plastic, glass, bio-waste, etc.
(C) Only one trash bin exists nationwide
(D) Recycling is illegal in Germany

question_en: What is 'Karneval/Fasching' in Germany?
options: (A) A solemn religious fasting period
(B) Pre-Lenten carnival season with parades, costumes, and revelry, especially in Rhineland
(C) An annual horse-racing festival
(D) A Christmas market tradition

question_en: When you sneeze in Germany, what is the typical response from others?
options: (A) Silence, as sneezes should not be acknowledged
(B) 'Gesundheit' (health) — wishing you good health
(C) An apology to the sneezer
(D) A handshake

question_en: In a German formal business email, how should you typically close?
options: (A) 'XOXO' or kisses
(B) 'Mit freundlichen Grüßen' (with friendly regards)
(C) 'Bye!' or 'See ya!'
(D) No closing needed

question_en: What does it mean when a German shop has a sign 'Sonntagsruhe'?
options: (A) Sunday discounts available
(B) Sunday rest — closed on Sundays per tradition and law
(C) Sunday-only special menu
(D) Sunday workers wanted

question_en: Why is the German train system Deutsche Bahn famous despite reliability complaints?
options: (A) German trains are always exactly on time
(B) Extensive network and the cultural value of punctuality makes any delay highly notable
(C) Trains in Germany do not actually exist
(D) Germans never ride trains

question_en: What is 'Stammtisch' in German social life?
options: (A) A type of strong coffee
(B) A regular reserved table at a pub for a group of friends/regulars to meet
(C) A formal political meeting
(D) A traditional dance

question_en: In Germany, the eldest person at a table typically:
options: (A) Must remain silent during the meal
(B) Is shown respect (e.g., seated first, served first), but rules vary by region
(C) Always pays for everyone
(D) Eats from a separate table

question_en: Why do Germans value 'Ordnung' (order)?
options: (A) It is required by German military code
(B) Cultural value emphasizing structure, rules, and predictability — 'Ordnung muss sein'
(C) Only practiced in Bavaria
(D) This stereotype is completely false

question_en: What is 'Kaffee und Kuchen' in German social culture?
options: (A) A breakfast meal eaten at 6 AM
(B) Afternoon coffee and cake tradition, typically around 15:00-16:00
(C) A formal business meeting
(D) A wedding ceremony ritual

question_en: When entering a small shop or elevator in Germany, what is polite?
options: (A) Remain silent; greetings are unnecessary
(B) Greet with 'Guten Tag' or 'Hallo' even to strangers
(C) Shake everyone's hand
(D) Announce your name loudly

question_en: Why is 'Beamter' (civil servant) a prestigious career path in Germany?
options: (A) Civil servants are paid extremely high salaries
(B) Lifetime job security, pension, and social respect for public service tradition
(C) Only nobility can become Beamter
(D) It is the only legal profession in Germany

question_en: Why do Germans typically prepare a 'Steuererklärung' (tax declaration)?
options: (A) It is purely optional and rarely done
(B) Many can reclaim taxes paid; common practice with cultural emphasis on financial precision
(C) It is only required for foreigners
(D) Germans do not pay taxes

question_en: What is the German concept of 'Datenschutz'?
options: (A) Free public Wi-Fi access
(B) Data protection — strong cultural and legal emphasis on personal data privacy
(C) A type of computer software
(D) A government surveillance program

question_en: In German bakery culture, what is typical of 'Brötchen'?
options: (A) Only available on weekends
(B) Daily fresh small bread rolls; many varieties; staple of breakfast
(C) A type of dessert pastry
(D) Imported from France

question_en: When invited to a German home, what gift is generally appropriate?
options: (A) A large appliance like a refrigerator
(B) Flowers (odd number, not red roses unless romantic), wine, or chocolates
(C) Live animals as pets
(D) Used clothing

question_en: What does 'Feierabend' mean in German workplace culture?
options: (A) A weekend office party
(B) End of the workday — a sacred boundary between work and personal time
(C) An emergency staff meeting
(D) Overtime pay

question_en: Why are 'Christmas markets' (Weihnachtsmärkte) significant in Germany?
options: (A) They are a recent commercial invention from the 2000s
(B) Centuries-old Advent tradition with Glühwein, crafts, and seasonal foods
(C) Only one Christmas market exists, in Berlin
(D) They are religious services held outdoors

question_en: In German driving culture, what is unique about the Autobahn?
options: (A) It is the only road in Germany
(B) Sections have no general speed limit; advisory 130 km/h; strict lane discipline
(C) Driving is illegal on the Autobahn
(D) Only military vehicles can use it

question_en: What is 'Heiligabend' in German Christmas tradition?
options: (A) New Year's Eve party
(B) Christmas Eve (Dec 24) — main gift-giving and family gathering day, not Dec 25
(C) Easter Sunday
(D) A Catholic confession ritual

question_en: Why do Germans typically book vacations far in advance?
options: (A) German law requires 12-month advance booking
(B) Long generous vacation allotment (typically 25-30 days/year) and value for planning
(C) Last-minute travel is banned
(D) Germans never go on vacation

question_en: When meeting Germans, what is the typical greeting handshake style?
options: (A) A very loose grip to show deference
(B) Firm, brief handshake with direct eye contact
(C) No handshake — hugs only
(D) Bow without physical contact

question_en: What is 'Walpurgisnacht' in German folklore?
options: (A) A national holiday for librarians
(B) Night of April 30 when witches were said to gather; celebrated with bonfires
(C) The longest day of summer
(D) A type of folk dance

question_en: In German restaurant culture, how do you typically request the bill?
options: (A) Stand up and walk to the cashier without asking
(B) Make eye contact with server and say 'Zahlen, bitte' or 'Die Rechnung, bitte'
(C) Whistle loudly
(D) Throw money on the table

question_en: Why is 'Pünktlichkeit' (punctuality) so emphasized in German culture?
options: (A) Tardiness incurs criminal penalties
(B) Strong cultural value linking punctuality with respect, reliability, and trustworthiness
(C) German clocks run faster than international time
(D) This stereotype is false

question_en: What is 'Kindergarten' literally and culturally in Germany?
options: (A) A type of vegetable garden
(B) 'Children's garden' — preschool tradition originating in Germany; ages ~3-6
(C) A summer camp for teenagers
(D) A government child welfare office

question_en: In Germany, why are 'Vereine' (clubs/associations) so popular?
options: (A) Membership is legally compulsory
(B) Strong tradition of organized civic life — clubs for sports, hobbies, music, charity
(C) Only one club exists in Germany
(D) Clubs are banned and operate illegally

question_en: What does the German phrase 'das ist nicht mein Bier' mean?
options: (A) 'I don't drink alcohol'
(B) 'That's not my problem/concern' (idiomatic)
(C) 'I prefer wine to beer'
(D) 'The beer is too cold'
